60,211 first touches of the open ± 0.5σ line on 34 instruments, 1,604 London sessions, Oct 2016 to Dec 2022 (2023 onward not loaded). Each is labelled fade and follow on six barrier shapes.

The barriers set the hit rate, not the market. Fade 1:1 at 0.25σ with a 2-hour limit: 38.6% hit the target first; a random walk with the same barriers and clock gives 41.7%. Among touches that hit a barrier: 50.2% [49.5, 51.0] vs exactly 50% for the random walk. 2:1: 32.7% vs 32.8%. 1:2: 67.8% vs 67.2%.

Real touches time out more than the random walk says (23% vs about 17% at 2 hours), on both sides equally. That is a vol shape effect (the average variance is inflated by bursts), not a direction effect.

Geometry alone gives AUC well above 0.5: pooling the six shapes 0.69 on a pure random walk, minutes left in the day 0.59. The purged 6-fold logistic reaches AUC 0.573 on real labels and 0.568 on random-walk labels run at each day's actual vol. Brier skill: +1.3% vs the base rate, -0.45% vs the geometry alone.

Target vs stop barely differ on any entry feature (gaps of 0.04σ-units or less); time-outs differ a lot (late, quiet, slow approach). A meta-model trained on target-first learns 'will this resolve', not 'which side wins'.

After one median spread (0.035σ) every quintile of the model's P loses about -0.03 to -0.05σ per trade, the top quintile most; taking every touch -0.041σ, a random 20% -0.040σ. To pay, the 1:1 2-hour fade needs +4.3pp over the random walk; 0.25σ held to 21:00 needs about +7pp.

Trades overlap: mean uniqueness 0.35, and the date-block variance is 3.5x the independent figure, so 60k touches are about 17k effective. Seeing 50% -> 53% needs 2,178 kept independent trades (5,186 after 100 trials), about 7,600 raw kept touches here.

Stable by year: the real-minus-random-walk gap is negative every year 2016-2022 (2h fade -1.6 to -5.7pp, all time-out driven). Only EURUSD and EURCHF sit above the random walk (+1.1pp each); crosses are lowest.
